commenti.body:
I was really into FNW directors at the time I watched it, but discipline was the key. Trying to watch an “episode” a day and honestly not thinking about the overall length but just taking it in moment-to-moment. It gets a bit easier to digest the further along you go, too. 

And it’s worth it, for anyone on the fence!

[This](https://jonathanrosenbaum.net/2021/08/out-1-and-its-double/) might be of value.  I disagree with some of it but it is a good place to start.  And perhaps watching Celine et Julie would be a way to ease one's self into a pertinent frame of mind.

Where did you watch it?  I’ve been wanting to watch it, but can’t find it anywhere.  It’s looks extremely interesting, and while the thirteen hour runtime is daunting to say the least, I really want to give it a shot and see how I like it.  I love French New Wave and all the new things those directors tried, so I’m really excited to see this movie.  I just have to find it first.

>what did you do in order to maximize your appreciation of it?

I had seen several other Rivette films before I watched it. That way it was more accessible because I already had an idea of what a Rivette film is like. So if anybody wants to watch it I would recommend watching some other films by Rivette first, he is a great filmmaker.
I got it through my local library's interlibrary loan service

I agree with others saying to watch other Rivette films first to get an idea of his themes and interests. 

I saw it in theaters over 3 days. The first episode with all the feet and theater exercises was rough but I was glad to not have distractions.

I saw it all in a theater in a single day. Fell asleep a bit during the second episode since I didn't sleep well enough the night before. As it was an Alamo Drafthouse, I was able to order coffee and food to keep me awake through the rest.

While I agree that it needs to be seen in a theater, one long ass day is not the way.
Damn that's crazy how often does the Alamo screen that lol?

I set aside a whole day to binge it. It was pretty amazing. Started to kind of go insane just like the characters did at the end. After so long watching basically nothing happening it's a real jolt when things start happening. The last two hours or so are still vivid in my mind.
